reasons: § 7.2 imposes an open-ended obligation on Customer to disclose and match any more favourable third-party offer for Vendor's benefit — squarely the rule's walk-away case and far short of the fallback (defined product, 12-month term, comparability carve-outs), so 'deviation' is correctly classified.

No Vendor-granted MFN exists in the cited text, so full deletion of p0026 removes only the burden on us and is the minimal edit reaching the preferred position, consistent with the redline guidance ('delete the obligation on Customer; keep any Vendor-granted MFN').

The redline is valid and self-consistent: the paragraph is removed entirely with no dangling references, and § 12.3 independently confirms no most-favoured-customer commitment was intended, so deletion improves internal consistency.

The comment is accurate, concise, in first person plural with the required [Playbook] prefix, states what changed and why, cites the playbook position, and notes MFN in our favour remains welcome; deterministic check passed.
